page.title: Downloads
page.description: Download the sanitised snapshot of the Webconsulting TYPO3 Lab: the database, the Fileadmin archive and a script that installs both in DDEV.

content.bodytext:
This is a complete copy of the lab. You get the database, the matching Fileadmin archive and a script that sets both up in a DDEV site.

Downloads

  • install.txt — setup script, run it with bash install.txt (3 KB)
  • db-public.zip — database, sanitised (10 MB)
  • fileadmin-public.zip — matching Fileadmin contents (352 MB)
  • snapshot-readme.txt — what is in the snapshot

Quick start

You need Docker or OrbStack, DDEV 1.25.3 or newer, and Git. The downloads ask for the same credentials you used to reach this page.

curl -fLO https://typo3-lab.webconsulting.at/fileadmin/_downloads/install.txt
bash install.txt

The script clones the repository, fetches both archives and runs the documented bootstrap. Sign in at /typo3/ with admin / Demo123*, then change that password.

The .txt and .zip extensions are deliberate. TYPO3 denies access to .sh and .sql files in the document root, and that rule should stay. The archives are zip files, not .tar.gz, because Apache serves any .gz file with Content-Encoding: gzip. Browsers then decode it without telling you. You would save a file named .tar.gz that is really a plain tar, and the import would reject it.

What “sanitised” means

The published database is not the one this site runs on. Twenty credential-bearing tables keep their structure but ship with no rows:

  • Vault secrets
  • API and MCP access tokens
  • OAuth records
  • WorkOS identities
  • the LLM provider credential
  • every backend and frontend account
  • the log and history tables

One demo administrator is added in their place.

Integrations that need credentials therefore start switched off. Add your own credentials in the Vault backend module.

Import the database and the Fileadmin archive together. The database references files by uid, so a mismatched pair shows broken images.
